items.answer: constant acceleration from rest

items.stem: A graph of V against I for a cell has gradient −0.80 Ω and y-intercept 1.52 V. What is the e.m.f.?
items.markingKey: V = E − Ir: intercept = E.

items.stem: A transmission cable has a constant resistance. The current is halved. State and explain how the power dissipated in the resistor changes.
items.answer: The power dissipated in the resistor becomes a quarter.
items.markingKey: Using P = I²R: power dissipated in the resistor ∝ current^2.00; factor = 0.500^2.00 = 0.250. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: A nucleus of ³₁H (nucleon number 3, proton number 1) undergoes β⁻ decay. What are the nucleon number and proton number of the daughter nucleus?
items.answer: nucleon number 3, proton number 2
items.markingKey: ³₁H → ³₂He + ⁰₋₁e + ν̄ₑ; nucleon and proton numbers balance.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Derive ΔE_p = mgΔh for an object lifted at constant speed. (b) Explain why a pendulum bob swinging in air eventually stops.
items.answer: (a) The lifting force equals the weight mg; work done = force × distance = mgΔh, which is stored as gravitational potential energy. (b) Work is done against air resistance (and friction at the pivot), so the mechanical energy is gradually transferred to thermal energy of the surroundings.
items.markingKey: (a) force = mg at constant speed [1]; W = mgΔh [1] [2] (b) work against air resistance/friction [1]; energy transferred to thermal [1] [2]

items.stem: A stone is thrown horizontally from a bridge at 12 m s⁻¹ from a height of 2.5 m above level ground. Air resistance is negligible. Calculate the time taken to reach the ground.
items.markingKey: h = ½gt² → t = √(2 × 2.5/9.81) = 0.714 s. (equation/substitution, then answer with unit) [3]

items.answer: 10⁻¹⁰ m

items.answer: Weight down, upthrust up (equal), thrust forwards larger than water resistance backwards.

A pressure sensor is held in a tank of liquid. The depth is increased by 50% while the density of the liquid stays the same. Explain how the pressure due to the liquid changes.

items.answer: f₀ = f_s v/(v + v_s)

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Show that the torque of a couple is the same about any point. (b) Explain why pushing a door at an angle to its surface is less effective than pushing perpendicularly.
items.answer: (a) Take a point a distance x from one force, separation d: moments are F(x + d) and −Fx; total = Fd, independent of x. (b) Only the component of force perpendicular to the door (F sin θ) produces a moment; the perpendicular distance from the hinge to the line of action is smaller.
items.markingKey: (a) moments about arbitrary point [1]; x cancels leaving Fd [1] [2] (b) only perpendicular component turns [1]; smaller moment for same force [1] [2]

items.stem: Samuel drives a delivery van along a straight road in Muscat at a constant 15 m s⁻¹ for 10 s, then brakes uniformly to rest in 8 s. (a) Calculate the distance travelled at constant speed. (b) Calculate the deceleration. (c) Calculate the average speed for the whole motion. (d) Explain why the average speed is less than the initial speed.
items.answer: (a) 150 m (b) 1.88 m s⁻² (c) 11.7 m s⁻¹ (d) During braking the van moves more slowly than its initial speed, so the total distance per unit time is reduced.
items.markingKey: (a) s = vt = 15 × 10: 150 m [1] (b) a = Δv/t = 15/8 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 1.88 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (c) 210/18 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 11.7 m s⁻¹ with unit [1] [2] (d) During braking the van moves more slowly than its initial speed, so the total distance per unit time is reduced [1]

items.stem: In an AS Physics lesson in Cairo, a 1.0 m length of nichrome wire of diameter 0.40 mm is used to find the resistivity of the alloy. (a) With a p.d. of 4.38 V the current is 0.50 A. Calculate the resistivity. (b) State the instrument used to measure the diameter and explain why several readings are taken. (c) Explain why the current should be kept small. (d) Distinguish between resistance and resistivity.
items.answer: (a) 1.10 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m (b) Micrometer screw gauge; the wire may not be uniform, and d is squared so its uncertainty matters. (c) A large current heats the wire, increasing its resistance (and resistivity). (d) Resistance depends on dimensions; resistivity is a property of the material.

items.stem: A brass wire 2.0 m long with diameter 0.40 mm is fixed to a ceiling beam and loaded with masses. (a) Define stress and strain. (b) Calculate the cross-sectional area of the wire. items.stem: Lina determines the resistivity of a metal wire using ρ = RA/L. The measurements are L = 1.000 ± 0.002 m, diameter d = 0.36 ± 0.01 mm and R = 5.6 ± 0.1 Ω. (a) Calculate the cross-sectional area of the wire. (b) Calculate the resistivity. (c) Explain why the micrometer should be checked for zero error before use.
items.answer: (a) 1.02 × 10⁻⁷ m² (b) 5.70 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m (c) A zero error is systematic and would shift every diameter reading, giving an inaccurate area and resistivity.
items.markingKey: (a) A = πd²/4 = π × (3.6 × 10⁻⁴)²/4 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 1.02 × 10⁻⁷ m² [1] [2] (b) ρ = RA/L = 5.6 × 1.02 × 10⁻⁷/1.000 (method/substitution) [1]; answer 5.70 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m [1] [2] (c) zero error systematic [1]; shifts all readings/affects ρ via d² [1] [2]

items.stem: A tractor of mass 1500 kg pulls a cart of mass 400 kg on a level track with a driving force of 3600 N. Resistive forces total 400 N and are shared in proportion to mass. (a) Calculate the acceleration of the system. (b) State Newton's third law and apply it to the tow bar. (c) Explain why the acceleration is less when the trailer is loaded with more mass.
items.answer: (a) 1.68 m s⁻² (b) If A exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force of the same type on A: the bar pulls the trailer forwards and the trailer pulls the car backwards with equal force. (c) For the same resultant force, a = F/m; a larger total mass gives a smaller acceleration.
items.markingKey: (a) a = (3600 − 400)/(1500 + 400) (method/substitution) [1]; answer 1.68 m s⁻² with unit [1] [2] (b) statement [1]; application [1] [2] (c) a = F/m [1]; larger mass [1] [2]

items.stem: A uniform gangplank of length 4.0 m and weight 300 N rests on a support at each end, A and B, at a port in Lima. (a) State the principle of moments. (b) A person of weight 600 N stands 3.0 m from A. Calculate the force at B. (c) Calculate the force at A. (d) Explain how the force at A changes as the person walks towards B. (e) Explain why the weight of a uniform board can be taken to act at its midpoint.
items.answer: (a) In equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about any point. (b) 600 N (c) 300 N (d) It decreases, because the moment of the person's weight about B decreases. (e) For a uniform board the centre of gravity is at its geometric centre.

items.answer: (a) The equation h = ½gt² assumes u = 0; a non-zero initial velocity would give an incorrect (smaller) time. (b) Measure t for several h; plot h against t²; g = 2 × gradient. (c) Air resistance; delay in release from the electromagnet; error in measuring h (wrong reference point).

items.stem: Engineers compare the force-extension behaviour of a steel cable, a rubber mounting and a ceramic rod. (a) Distinguish between elastic and plastic deformation.
